source_title: 'Ramayana': Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, and Sai Pallavi attend the film’s world premiere in US ahead of theatrical release - The Hindu
source_excerpt: 'Ramayana': Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, and Sai Pallavi attend the film’s world premiere in US ahead of theatrical release center Namit Malhotra, Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, Yash and Nitesh Tiwari at the red carpet of the world premiere of ‘Ramayana’ at Los Angeles on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) Getty Images Getty Images https://th-i.thgim.com/public/entertainment/movies/1foctq/article71634890.ece/alternates/FREE_1200/cvr%20-%202026-10-28T131653.755.jpg The star-studded world premiere of ‘Ramayana’ was organised at the David Geffen Theatre of the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in Los Angeles. The first part of Ramayana, starring Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi as Ram and Sita, had its star-studded world premiere at the David Geffen Theatre of the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in Los Angeles on Tuesday (October 27, 2026). 'Ramayana' Part 1 to release worldwide on November 5; advance bookings to open on Dussehra storyline 1 ‘OM – Chapter 1’: Sai Pallavi is IPS Nithya Reddy in Dhanush-Rajkumar Periasamy’s next storyline 1 Ranbir, Pallavi, producer Namit Malhotra, director Nitesh Tiwari and actor-producer Yash attended the gala evening on Tuesday at the prestigious venue that has hosted premieres of leading Hollywood movies in the past. ‘Ramayana’: AR Rahman, Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi on bringing the epic to life ‘Ramayana’: AR Rahman, Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi on bringing the epic to life With music by AR Rahman and Hans Zimmer, the two-part epic promises a grand retelling of the Ramayana ‘Ramayana’: AR Rahman, Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi on bringing the epic to life storyline 1 Produced by Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with his company DNEG and Yash's Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is being touted as the most ambitious Indian production ever with a reported combined budget of over Rs 4,000 crore for both the parts. Envisioned as a two-part cinematic epic, the film also features Yash as Ravana and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. At the premiere, Yash spoke about the cultural and generational significance of Ramayana, which has been a part of Indian storytelling tradition for centuries. "Where you start can never define how far you can go. Today, I am proud of being a member of the Kannada film industry, telling our story, which is not just a story. "In our country, we just don't tell the story, we remember it, and we pass it down for generations to come and this story has travelled for thousands of years," Yash said. Ahead of the film's world premiere, Malhotra told PTI that it was a great moment to showcase the story to the world on such a grand scale. "I think it's the ultimate moment for Indian cinema overall. In over a hundred years (of Indian cinema), it's one thing to say that there's a screening and the other is to say that there's a whole city in the US, which has Ramayana hoardings all over," he said. ‘Ramayana’ VFX criticism: Yash slams social media hate ‘Ramayana’ VFX criticism: Yash slams social media hate After the first ‘Ramayana’ trailer drew heat for its visual effects, actor Yash, who plays Ravana in the mythological epic, has defended the visuals as the movie gears up for a November 5 release ‘Ramayana’ VFX criticism: Yash slams social media hate storyline 1 The producer said the film's US screening is not just aimed at creating curiosity but also credibility. "This is a massive spectacle coming out of India about one of the greatest epics and a Hollywood studio that's distributing it. We've got some of the top Indian talent, some of the top Western talent, and they are all coming together to make something that's never been done before, at a budget and scale. Again, that is unique to anything the rest of the world makes... It has several firsts attached to its name, and I believe the visibility and centre stage we hope to achieve for 'Ramayana' and Indian cinema go hand in hand," he said. The first instalment of Ramayana is scheduled for a worldwide theatrical release on November 5, 2026, while the second part is expected to arrive during Diwali 2027. The film will be released in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam, with an IMAX release also planned. Sony Pictures will handle the film's international distribution outside India, while Dharma Productions will distribute it in the Hindi-speaking market. The film's star-studded cast also includes Sunny Deol, Anupam Kher, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Kunal Kapoor, Adinath Kothare, Arun Govil, Indira Krishnan and Lara Dutta.
